prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Design Your Companion's Personality", "Select Pet Trait & Appearance"]
1: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Adoption Seal Verified"]
2: ["Your Companion is Ready on Your Desktop!", "Learn Quick Controls: Summon, Hide & Feed"]
3: ["Signing in with your account automatically restores your saved pets and progress."]
4: ["Preview Companion Abilities", "Your companion can walk across your taskbar, fetch items, and react to your activity.", "Continue to Adoption"]
5: ["Desktop Quick Start Checklist", "Complete these 3 quick actions to master your desktop pet.", "1. Click pet to interact | 2. Right-click for menu | 3. Drag to move"]
6: ["Preparing Your Pet's New Home"]
7: ["Choose How to Create Your Companion", "Instant Companion vs Custom AI Photo Pet"]
8: ["Tip: Look for the pet icon in your system tray (bottom right corner) to access controls anytime."]
9: ["Use a clear, full-body photo of your pet with good lighting and a distinct background for best results."]
